symptom: An attribute used only through a document's own parameter in an expression (`$Card/Title` in a snippet text-template parameter, a page widget, a microflow or nanoflow split) was in no reference: `show references to Shop.Card.Title` was empty, so MDL108 passed `alter entity … drop attribute` and `mx check` then reported CE0117 on each. The issue called it a snippet gap; page expressions and microflow expressions had it too, and only widget bindings and `change` members (stored as qualified names) were found.
file: mdl/catalog/builder_member_refs.go: documentParameterEntities, memberRefIndex.vars, resolvePath's `$` case. Tests: builder_member_refs_vars_test.go
cause: resolvePath set the context to "" for every `$variable` segment, because a variable's type was not known — a limit the file's header documents. A document's own parameters DO declare their entity (Forms$PageParameter / Forms$SnippetParameter `ParameterType`, Microflows$MicroflowParameter `VariableType`, each a DataTypes$ObjectType), so the walk can know it.
insight: **The issue's own evidence pointed at the wrong class.** It listed snippets as the gap and pages as covered, because it compared a snippet's expression use with a page's widget binding. Reproducing the same expression on a page and a microflow showed the gap was `$var/Attr` everywhere; the control was putting the identical use in all three document types. The fix resolves only a document's declared parameters and leaves retrieve results, loop items and a data view's object unresolved — those need real variable typing — and a reference graph that is silent there still gives MDL108 the same blind spot for them.
